text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone proves nothing. Planning and public-sector HR skew female, so a four-woman panel is statistically unremarkable — you'd expect it reasonably often by chance. Raising it would make you look aggrieved and would overshadow your stronger point.

The real anomaly is substantive: a director role filled by someone with less formal qualification than you. But directorships often weight political instincts, council relations and consultation skills over technical depth — and two interviews mean they assessed you directly, not just your CV.

Do pursue the written explanation. Chase it in writing, citing any policy or statutory deadline. Ask for your interview scoring. If the feedback is evasive or the stated criteria weren't in the posting, you have a procedural grievance — a far better footing than guessing at motive.
